Who Was Evicted From ‘Big Brother’ Australia? The Complete 2026 List

Grab the tissues and say your goodbyes
Ruby Feneley
24 November, 2026

THE RUNDOWN

  • Big Brother Australia 2026 evictions are in motion, with evictions taking place on Sunday at 7:00 pm AEDT.
  • Viewers can save their favourite nominated housemates from the chopping block by casting their votes through the official Big Brother Voting Portal on 10Play ahead of Sunday’s live eviction.
  • Week 4 saw Heath and Charity eliminated, and in Week 5, intruders Evie and Tara are up for eviction alongside Anita.

Another two bite the dust on Big Brother Australia. On Sunday night, Charity and Heath were evicted in a surprising move that saw some fellow contestants delighted (Ebony) and others sad to see them go. This week, two of the three recent intruders, Tara and Evie, are up for elimination after clashing with both each other and their housemates.

The 2026 season of Big Brother Australia has resembled Game of Thrones more than a reality show. Pam was sent packing during Phoebe’s 26th birthday week, then Phoebe was sent to the chopping block by her best friend, Ebony after she chose to save controversial Matthew instead of her. Matthew met his untimely demise in Week Three anyway, when his housemates grew tired of his probing and pot-stirring and showed him the door. Marshy was eliminated in a shock twist, and Heath and Charity were evicted at once in a swift double elimination. In this game, loyalty doesn’t count for much.

Now, in Week Five of the show, intruders Evie and Tara are up for elimination after failing to gel with their fellow contestants and each other, for that matter. Anita, widely perceived as a major threat, is also on the chopping block. Somehow, controversial housemate Ebony has managed to dodge the threat of elimination once again, despite rubbing more than one of her peers the wrong way.

Related: Get Up Close With All 14 ‘Big Brother’ Australia 2026 Housemates

Advertisement

Despite losing seven housemates, the addition of three intruders means 10 housemates still remain in the Big Brother house, and we’ll be keeping track of every contentious eviction. It airs tonight on Channel 10.

How To Vote For A Housemate On Big Brother Australia

Vote to save your favourite housemate from elimination through the Big Brother Voting Portal on 10Play. For more details, like how to vote in challenges, have a look at our guide.

Who Is Up For Eviction On Big Brother Australia?

This week, three housemates are up for eviction, including our two freshly-inducted intruders:

  • Anita
  • Tara
  • Evie

Who Was Evicted From Big Brother Australia?

Heath

Advertisement

When Heath was announced as the seventh housemate to leave Big Brother, his fellow contestants responded with appropriately sombre reactions. All of them, except Ebony, who sat cheering on the couch. When the other housemates attempted to pull her into line, she shot back, “No, he said he wants me out so it’s tit-for-tat.” Heath got his payback in his farewell interview, saying, “Ebony, Ebony, Ebony. You are fake. You are manipulative. You are so incredibly frustrating.” Suffice to say, these two will not be remaining in touch.

Charity

On Sunday night, Charity became the sixth housemate to leave the Big Brother house, and she blames her untimely eviction on her fellow housemate, Matthew. In an interview with Chattr, Charity believes that when Matthew — a friend of hers in the house — left a video message for the housemates saying she was “playing the game” and hinting that she was “under-the-radar,” it opened their eyes to the threat she posed to their own chances of victory. Lo and behold, Charity received the least number of votes and was shown the door, but she handled it like a champion, telling her fellow housemates, “Don’t worry, I had a dream about it.”

Marshy

A peaceful meditation circle lost all its zen when Big Brother co-opted it to pull a surprise elimination on Marshy. As the housemates sat in a circle listening to a guided meditation through noise-cancelling headphones, Big Brother interrupted the broadcast to let them know Marshy had received the boot, but forgot to clue Marshy in on his eviction. As the contestants sat dumbfounded, they had to wait for Marshy to open his eyes before letting him know he was no longer welcome in the Big Brother abode.

Matthew

A mere few hours after his elimination, Matthew took to TikTok Live, where he asked his followers for some “hard-hitting” questions to “stir the pot.” This was Matthew’s whole schtick: pushing buttons, getting a rise out of the contestants and occasionally throwing them under the bus. It might be how he struck up such a friendship with fellow drama-maker, Ebony. It worked until it didn’t, ending in his ultimate dismissal, which left Evie in tears.

Phoebe

Advertisement

On Sunday night, poor Phoebe became the third housemate to exit the Big Brother Australia house. She took the eviction on the chin, confirming her plans to eat a Nutella sandwich on release. It didn’t take long after her exit for Phoebe to start spilling the tea about the fractious group dynamics in the Big Brother house, particularly Ryan and Matthew’s brewing conflict. “There’s definitely a divide,” she told Who. “There was an initial small divide, and like everyone was kind of figuring it out.

But I think after the Maltesers event, there has been a big divide in the house.” Phoebe herself struck up a friendship with Ebony, but Ebony turned traitor when, in her role as Head Housemate, she chose to save Matthew from eviction instead of Phoebe. This left Phoebe vulnerable, and when she received the fewest Save Votes during a live red button twist, she was booted. She had a few parting words for her former friend Ebony as she exited: “Oh girl, I hope you feel guilty.”

We’ll have to wait and see.

Pam

Advertisement

While Phoebe’s birthday started with pass the parcel, it sadly ended in a surprise elimination for Pam. Indeed, it was such a surprise that poor Pam didn’t even get to pack any of her stuff! “It was the worst pass the parcel ever, and I’ve been to a few pass the parcels,” Pam told Pedestrian TV ruefully. While Pam was the house’s resident mediator and spent a lot of time diffusing conflict amongst the housemates, some, like Kyrah, were brought to tears by the exit. Thoughtful to the end, Pam tried to put a brave face on it because “otherwise it was going to degenerate into the worst game of pass the parcel of humankind,” she told PTV. You’ll be missed, Pam!

Harmon (Evicted November 1)

 Harmon’s time in the house was turbulent from the start. True to his word of pushing buttons, he deliberately hid the house’s supply of coffee and salt to shake up what he saw as a boring dynamic. “They’re just a bit too comfy in there… it’s not school camp!” he later explained to host Mel Tracina. “We’re in there to have a good time, it’s meant to be tough, and it just wasn’t tough.” The stunt severely backfired, resulting in him feeling “almost exiled” and “shunned from the village” by the rest of the cast. Harmon went out with a bang, delivering a savage goodbye message that targeted his fellow contestants before using his exit power to crown Ebony as the next Head of House. Standing by his brutal parting words, he noted: “You can’t just leave going, ‘Oh yeah, you’re all nice. Have a good day.’ … You gotta have a go and you have to get under their skin a bit. Even when I’m gone, they’ll be thinking about me.”
